territorial_scope.description: Directs U.S. federal agencies (NSF and NIST) to carry out research, standards and reporting activities.

evidence.quote: The Director of the National Science Foundation, in consultation with other relevant Federal agencies, shall support merit-reviewed and competitively awarded research

summary.short: Directs the National Science Foundation to fund research on manipulated or synthesized content, including GAN-generated deepfakes, and the National Institute of Standards and Technology to support measurement research and voluntary standards for GANs. Requires a joint NSF-NIST report on public-private detection partnerships within one year of enactment.
summary.long: The Identifying Outputs of Generative Adversarial Networks Act (IOGAN Act), approved December 23, 2020, addresses research on generative adversarial networks (GANs) and comparable techniques that create or manipulate content. Section 3 directs the National Science Foundation, in consultation with other relevant Federal agencies, to support merit-reviewed, competitively awarded research on manipulated or synthesized content and information authenticity, covering digital forensic tools, watermarking, social and behavioral research, public awareness research, and awards coordinated with DARPA and IARPA. Section 4 directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology to support research on measurements and standards for GANs and other content-synthesizing technologies, to conduct outreach to stakeholders, and to consider the feasibility of ongoing public and private engagement on voluntary standards. Section 5 requires NSF and NIST to jointly submit, within one year of enactment, a report to specified congressional committees on the feasibility of research with the private sector, including digital media companies, and on policy recommendations for coordination. Section 6 defines generative adversarial network. The operative provisions impose duties on federal agencies; they do not set obligations, thresholds or penalties for private parties.

notes: Only the relations section was requested. The text cites no other instrument by name or number and states no legal basis. The Networking and Information Technology Research and Development Program, NSF, NIST, DARPA and IARPA are bodies or programs, not instruments, so they are not coded. The text gives only 'Approved December 23, 2020' with no bill number, so no enacted_by_bill relation is recorded. The Sec. 5 report deadline runs from the date of enactment, which the text does not state as a date.

events.applies_to: Joint report by the NSF Director and NIST Director to the specified House and Senate committees (SEC. 5)

relations.note: No relation to another instrument is stated in the text. Named agencies and programs are not instruments.

thresholds.note: The Act directs NSF and NIST to support research and standards and requires a report. It sets no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment of any person. The only number tied to an operative provision is the 1-year report deadline in Sec. 5, a procedural time limit recorded as an event, not a threshold.
